title: Typed Checkpointing and Mobile Prefetch Playbook
content:
Purpose
This doc collects design notes, edge cases, and rollout guidance for a combined feature set: typed checkpointing (resumable incremental output), opportunistic prefetch for mobile SDKs, and lightweight tool-call handshake semantics for low-bandwidth environments. Goal is an ergonomic SDK surface that minimizes perceived latency for flaky networks while keeping server-side cost predictable and preserving structured output guarantees.

Context / Motivation
- Mobile clients suffer from variable latency and intermittent connectivity. Long-running streamed responses are frequently interrupted, causing poor UX or wasted tokens.
- We already support streaming partial output and tool calling, but clients today either buffer everything or retry from scratch, which is expensive.
- Introducing typed checkpoints (compact, verifiable resume tokens with a small amount of state) enables clients to resume from a known point and rehydrate partial results without re-running entire model work.
- Combined with a short prefetch window for likely follow-up tokens and a clearly typed tool-handshake, we can reduce roundtrips and client-perceived latency while maintaining deterministic structured responses for downstream tool execution.

High-level user stories
- As a mobile developer, I want the SDK to resume a partial streamed response after a network hiccup without re-requesting the full generation so that my users don't see duplicate content or long waits.
- As a product owner, I want predictable cost behavior: resume tokens should not allow infinite recomputation or double-billing for completed tokens.
- As an SDK engineer, I want a small, explicit API so app developers can opt into prefetch heuristics and control tool-call safety boundaries.

Non-goals
- This is not a full offline-first persistent conversation store (we rely on app storage for snapshots).
- Not providing strong cryptographic guarantees beyond signing/resume-ids for integrity (no end-to-end encryption change in this RFC).

Design principles
- Typed: resume checkpoints carry a small typed payload (schema id + offset + optional KV checkpoint pointer) to enable server verification and backward-compatible evolution.
- Minimum server memory: checkpoints are compact references; server may lazily reconstruct from cached KV or from a short execution trace but should not require long-lived per-session state for months.
- Client-first ergonomics: the SDK exposes simple primitives (onFragment, onCheckpoint, resumeFrom, prefetchHint) rather than forcing developers to manage frames and tokens.
- Cost-aware: resumed work is charged only for tokens generated during resumed execution; completed tokens bound to checkpoint are not charged twice.

API surface (sketch)
- SDK methods (pseudocode):
  - startStream(request, {onFragment, onCheckpoint, onToolCall})
  - resumeStream(resume_token, {onFragment, onCheckpoint, onToolCall})
  - prefetchHint(resume_token, lookahead: 8)
- Resume token (opaque string) encodes: version|model_id|seq_offset|signed_hash. Server verifies signature and sequence offset before resuming.

Checkpoint semantics
- Checkpoint emitted periodically (configurable cadence: default every 256 tokens or on structured-boundary events).
- Checkpoint payload: schema_version, model_version, token_offset, last_frame_id, tool_state_digest (if any), optional short KV pointer key (<= 64 chars).
- Checkpoint is signed by server key; clients store token+human-friendly small JSON summary returned in-stream.
- Resuming: client calls resumeStream(token). Server validates, reconstructs KV/context within a bounded window, reinstates last_frame_id and continues generation from token_offset.

Tool-call handshake in resumed/low-bandwidth cases
- Problem: tool-calls often require exact prior state (arguments, partial entities). Resuming ahead of a pending tool-call could lead to replay or loss.
- Proposal: tool-calls are declared stable only after an explicit commit frame. Until commit, tool-call frames are part of ephemeral stream state and cannot be re-executed after resume without confirmation.
- When a tool-call is issued in-stream, server emits a tool_frame and a corresponding checkpoint that includes tool_state_digest. If resume occurs and the digest indicates commit==false, SDK prompts app developer callback (onStalledTool) to decide: re-run tool or discard.

Prefetch heuristics for mobile
- Prefetch window: server may opportunistically generate and cache up to N tokens (default 8–16) past emitted fragments when network conditions are detected as cellular/high-latency or when client requests prefetchHint. These tokens are ephemeral and result in one of three outcomes: consumed, discarded, or used as seed on resume (not double-charged if they were not sent to client).
- Client controls: max_prefetch_tokens, prefetch_timeout_ms, prefetch_policy = {opportunistic, conservative, disabled}.
- Cost rule: prefetch tokens are not billed unless they are attached to a served fragment or used to seed resumed generation that emits them to the client. We must instrument billing to account for this policy (see Telemetry below).

Structured output guarantees
- We want clients to be able to rely on stable JSON-ish frames even across resumptions. To that end:
  - Fragment boundaries should map to typed frames (frame_type: narrative|json-object|tool-call|commit).
  - Checkpoints emitted at frame boundaries enable deterministic reassembly on the client.
  - Server guarantees idempotent frame IDs (UUIDv4 prefixed by model_id) so clients can dedupe when reapplying fragments after resume.

Telemetry and observability (must have)
- Events to emit:
  - stream.start (tags: model, client_sdk_version, network_type_hint)
  - fragment.emitted (frame_id, fragment_length, checkpoint_included: boolean)
  - checkpoint.issued (checkpoint_id, token_offset, emits_since_last_checkpoint)
  - resume.attempt (resume_token_present, success, reason_if_fail)
  - prefetch.requested (policy, tokens_requested, network_hint)
  - prefetch.outcome (consumed|discarded|reused_on_resume, tokens_count)
  - tool.call.pending (tool_id, commit_flag)
  - tool.call.resolved (tool_id, resolution: success|retry|discard)
- Dashboards: check resumed stream success rate, average tokens wasted to prefetch, ratio of resumed streams that required manual tool resolution. Alert if resume.failures > 1% or prefetch_waste_tokens_ratio > 0.2.

Billing & cost controls
- Recorded guideline only (ops needs sign-off): Add billing dimension resume_seeded_tokens. Policy: prefetch tokens are free unless they are included in final delivered tokens post-resume or are explicitly consumed by SDK.
- Hard quota: allow customers to set resume-prefetch budget per project to avoid runaway prefetch experiments. Token breach triggers throttling (policy configurable: block_prefetch | degrade_prefetch_rate | notify).

Backward compatibility and migration
- Versioned resume token: tokens contain version header; older clients that don't understand typed checkpointing will ignore checkpoint frames (server keeps serving streaming fragments normally).
- Server-side: for models that do not support KV checkpoint pointers, resume will fall back to replay-from-last-committed-frame (slower, higher cost) and server returns a resume_hint explaining degraded resume fidelity.

SDK ergonomics and sample flows
- Basic streaming (no resume): startStream -> (onFragment x N) -> complete
- Streaming with checkpoints and resume: startStream -> onFragment + onCheckpoint(save token summary) -> network drop -> resumeStream(token) -> onFragment (deduped via frame_id)
- Tool-call case: onToolCall(tool_frame) -> client may confirm tool execution -> server emits commit frame -> checkpoint includes commit flag -> subsequent resume is safe to auto-execute tool results

Mobile-specific UX patterns (notes to product/design)
- Show progress with stable fragments rather than token-by-token flicker; rehydrate fragments on resume using their frame_id to avoid jumps.
- When a partial tool result exists (commit==false), show a soft blocker: "Action pending — retry?" with small contextual info from tool_state_digest instead of raw tool body.

Operational concerns and edge cases
- Malicious resume_token replay attempts: token signed, short TTL (default 24h), tie token to project_id and model_version. Allow customer-managed signing option for Private deployments.
- Checkpoint growth: some flows produce many checkpoints (chatty apps). Provide adaptive cadence: if client frequently resumes within Xs, increase checkpoint frequency; otherwise, reduce to save bandwidth.
- Cross-device resume: tokens are portable across devices if allowed by customer policy; risky for PII — default: tokens are single-device unless project settings permit sharing.

Rollout plan (phased)
1) Internal beta: enable platform+console flag, SDK experimental toggle for iOS/Android/JS, telemetry-only mode for prefetch decisions. 2 weeks.
2) Pilot customers: 2–3 mobile-first customers opt-in. Collect metrics on resume success and prefetch waste. 6 weeks.
3) Wider opt-in: enable feature by default for mobile SDK minor version bump; allow orgs to disable. 8 weeks.
4) GA and billing activation: finalize billing semantics with finance, migrate prefetch billing to live accounting and enable quota controls. 4 weeks.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- SDKs can emit and consume resume tokens with documented API and clear sample apps.
- Server validates tokens, resumes within bounded cost (95th percentile additional tokens < 1.5x baseline for resumed flows).
- Telemetry dashboards show resume.success_rate >= 98% for pilot customers and prefetch_waste_tokens_ratio < 0.15.

Open questions / TODOs
- TTL: what is the default resume token TTL for hosted vs dedicated vs private? (ops/legal)
- Billing edge cases: prefetch tokens that are used to seed a resumed generation — how do we prevent double billing when partial fragments were already delivered? Need billing & infra design.
- Commit semantics: do we allow explicit tool.commit API that app devs call to mark tool output permanent? (UX + SDK change)
- Security: should we allow customer-sponsored signing keys for resume tokens in Redwood Private? (SRE + security)

References and links
- Confluence: /pages/CONFLUENCE-3452 (design log)
- Jira epic: JIRA-1129 (mobile-resume-prefetch)
- SDK PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk#pr-78 (prototype iOS/Android patches)

Notes to implementer
- Keep resume token decode on server-side lightweight — prefer verifier that checks signed metadata and then reads minimal KV pointers. Avoid keeping long-lived handle tables keyed by tokens.
- Add a v1->v2 migration compatibility test in the streaming integration suite: issue v1 token, upgrade server, confirm resume_hint returned when fidelity degrades.

Appendix: Example resume token payload (human-friendly, returned alongside opaque string)
{
  "schema_version": "1",
  "model_id": "rwd-llama-2-13b-v0",
  "token_offset": "256",
  "last_frame_id": "frame_20241120_9b8f",
  "tool_state_digest": "sha256:...",
  "expires_at": "2024-12-05T18:00:00Z"
}

( SDK stores only the opaque token + this small JSON summary for display and quick heuristics )

Endnotes
This is a sketch — prioritized around mobile first because the latency/interrupt pattern is the most painful UX. Feedback requested from infra (KV pointer size limit), billing (prefetch accounting), security (token TTL & customer keys), and SDK (API names and ergonomics).

-- Asha
